sentences.text: Hemant Kumar Vaishnav and Shri Sahitya Vaishna  for the appellants.
Shri Monesh Jindal, learned counsel for the respond  ORDER Heard on I.A. No.9088/2025, an application for dispensing with the service of notice upon respondent No.1.
In view of the fact that liability is not under dispute, application is allowed.
Service on respondent No.1 is hereby dispensed with.
2. With consent of the parties, the matter is being heard finally.

3 . The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 19.11.2019 passed in claim case No.185/2017 challenging the quantum of compensation.

4. The short facts of the case are that on 12.02.2016 at around 05 a.m., deceased Shraddha @
Sonum was returning along with her brother Sourabh and father Mahendra from Ratlam to Sailana after attending a marriage ceremony by vehicle XUV 500 bearing registration number MP43-CA-5112.

The respondent No.1 was driving the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner,
when they reached near Banjali T-point (Tiraaha) in front of medical college gate at Sailana Road the same NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32073 2 MA-1175-2020 got upturned because of which the persons sitting in the vehicle, including deceased Shraddha, sustained grievous injuries.
They were rushed to government hospital, Ratlam where Shraddha was declared dead by the medical officer.
5. The appellants/claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the death of Shraddha.

The claims tribunal after recording evidence Mahendra Kumar vs Premsingh on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193791152/
1 concluded that the deceased Shraddha died due to accident caused by rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle and consequently, total compensation of Rs.3,93,000/- was awarded to the appellants by the claims tribunal 6.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal while assessing income of the deceased has discarded claim of her earning of Rs.20,000/- per month and assessed her income on notional basis at Rs.30,000/-
per annum.

He points out that in fact, the claims tribunal has completely ignored the documents regarding educational qualification of the deceased which would show that she was not only a bright student but was on the verge of securing lucrative employment owing to the fact that she had already cleared the initial part of CA examination and was slated to become qualified CA.
He, for demonstrating the educational progress of the deceased, refers to Ex.P-11 to Ex.P-18 which are mark-sheets of the deceased.
He points out mark-sheet of the deceased for higher secondary in which she has secured first division and of B.Com. in which she has also received goods marks.
Ex.P-24 is the admit card for CA examination and Ex.P-25 is the mark-sheet of Group-I and Group-II.
He thus submits that the claims tribunal has erred in considering the income of the deceased at Rs.3000/- per annum by treating her as unskilled labourer.
He thus prays for enhancement of the compensation for loss of earning.

He further submits that apart from this,
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:32073 3 MA-1175-2020 nothing has been awarded for loss of consortium although the claimants are mother and father of the deceased Shraddha.
He also points out that nothing has been awarded for loss of estate.
He thus prays for over all enhancement in the compensation.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company submits that the claims tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased.

He points out to Ex.P-21 the mark-sheet of third semester of B.Com. and submits that she has only received 51% marks in the said examination which would show that she was not a bright student and Ex.P-25 which is the mark sheet of her CA examination first part, in which she has secured 50% marks .
He tried to demonstrate that the deceased was not a bright student and there was no certainty that she would have cleared CA examination and ultimately would have become a qualified CA.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9.
From perusal of the documents Ex.P-11 to Ex.P-26, this Court has no doubts that the deceased Shraddha was a bright student.

She has not only secured first division in classes 10th and 12th but has also secured on most of the occasions marks commensurate to first division in her B.Com.
examination.
She had cleared first phase of CA examination also.
As such, this Court has no hesitation in holding that the deceased was having a bright career ahead of her.

Considering the same and also in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Deepak Singh @ Deepak Chauhan Vs. Mukesh and others, 2025 SCC OnLine SC 277, the income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the claimants are mother and father of the deceased, both of them are hereby awarded Rs.40,000/- each.
A further amount of Rs.15,000/- is awarded for loss of estate.
After above said addition in the amount of compensation and modification in the income, the total amount of compensation would now come to Rs.16,22,000/-.

After deducting already awarded amount of Rs.3,93,000/-, the appellants are now entitled for compensation of Rs.12,29,000/- which shall be paid to them with interest @6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.
11. From the record, it is seen that the appeal has been valued at Rs.10 Lacs and the appellants are required to pay deficit court fees within a period of eight weeks from today.
In absence of which the interest shall not apply on enhanced amount beyond the period of eight weeks.
12. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands allowed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
